Programme Overview





Students with a science background can pursue a career in physiotherapy. To practice as a physiotherapist or work professionally in a hospital or clinic, one must have a Bachelor's degree. The course provides students with a fundamental understanding of the human body based on medical sciences and training in therapy procedures and related skills. Course topics include anatomy, physiology, pathology, pharmacology, psychology, medical and surgical conditions, biomechanics, kinesiology, disability prevention, rehabilitation, and others. The course includes practical components, such as an internship where students work under professional supervision at various hospitals and institutions. Good interpersonal skills are important for physiotherapy as it is a patient-centered field. To excel, a physiotherapist must have strong analytical and logical reasoning, scientific reasoning and problem-solving skills, the ability to memorize and recall scientific facts, manual dexterity, physical stamina, patience, a sympathetic approach, a desire to help people, level-headedness to handle emergencies, mental and emotional fortitude, teamwork, good observation skills, and the ability to instill confidence in patients. These traits, combined with a thorough knowledge of anatomy, are key to success in physiotherapy.






Programme Educational Objectives





Any Physiotherapy Graduates will be well prepared for successful careers as physiotherapists in one or more of the sectors: hospitals, rehabilitation centres, academic institutions, sports clubs, NGOs, government schemes etc.
Physiotherapy graduates will be academically prepared to become licensed physiotherapy practitioners and will contribute effectively to the growth and development of the healthcare profession, and the society at large.
The graduates will engage in professional practices to enhance their physiotherapeutic skill and stature, establish physiotherapy clinics or rehabilitation centres, and be successful in higher education if pursued

Apply knowledge of musculoskeletal, neurological and cardiopulmonary fundamental and physiotherapy techniques for treatment and rehabilitation of individuals suffering from different health conditions.
Analyze complex clinical scenarios adopting evidence-based practices and critical thinking to provide optimum physiotherapeutic care

Communicate effectively and exhibit interpersonal skills fostering collaborative relationships with patients, healthcare teams and other stakeholders in a diversified healthcare system.
Incorporate ethical principles into professional practice to ensure the provision of physiotherapy services that consider cultural diversity and uphold individual autonomy with respect.

Proficient in utilizing modern technology and tools for assessment, diagnosis and treatment planning in physiotherapy practice.
Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in a diverse team of multiple medico professionals for an active role as a physiotherapist in healthcare promotion and prevention initiatives.

Engage in lifelong learning staying abreast of advancements in physiotherapy and technical advancements to continually enhance clinical competence in evolving healthcare landscapes

MBBS isn't the only option: explore rewarding healthcare careers without NEET


Date- 13th Aug 2026



Medical courses that don’t require NEET are in high demand - Pharmacy, Nursing, and several Allied Health paths have long welcomed students this way, though 2026-27 brings new entry rules worth knowing before you choose.

Is MBBS the Only Option for Your Healthcare Career?

Not even close. India's healthcare system runs on a workforce far wider than doctors alone the country has just over a quarter of the WHO-recommended 44.5 skilled health workers per 10,000 people, and the Union Budget 2026-27 alone set aside Rs. 1,000 crore to add a lakh new allied and healthcare professionals over the next five years. Every year, lakhs of NEET aspirants compete for a comparatively small number of MBBS seats, which means most students exploring a medical career are, by definition, looking at options beyond MBBS anyway. The healthcare system needs pharmacists, nurses, radiographers, physiotherapists, lab scientists, and dialysis technicians just as urgently as it needs doctors.

What If You Don't Clear NEET?

Not clearing NEET, or choosing not to sit for it, doesn't close the door on a healthcare career. Pharmacy remains a genuinely NEET-free professional route, regulated separately by the Pharmacy Council of India. Nursing has long welcomed students through state-level entrance tests or direct merit at most institutions. And Allied Health Sciences - the professionals who run diagnostics, imaging technology, rehabilitation, and clinical support etc are in the middle of a government-backed expansion, with the sector needing to more than double its current strength of professionals to meet the current demand. It's worth knowing the name itself has changed too - the term "Paramedical" has been officially replaced by "Allied and Healthcare" across India, following a 2025 government directive requiring every institution to adopt the new terminology.

Which Professional Healthcare Courses One Can Pursue Without NEET?
If you are searching for allied health sciences courses without NEET, this last row is the one to read twice: NCAHP's rollout is happening in phases, and not every institution or course is affected yet, so it's worth confirming the current, course-specific entry requirement directly with the university before you plan around it.

Why Are Allied Healthcare Career Options Gaining Popularity in India?

The demand side of this story is hard to overstate. India has roughly 12-13 lakh allied health professionals today against an estimated need of 25-30 lakh, a shortfall north of 10 lakh workers. The government's response - Rs. 1,000 crore to add a lakh new professional over five years, plus new AHP training institutes across 10 disciplines including optometry, radiology, anesthesia, and OT technology - signals just how seriously this gap is being taken. Beyond policy, the sector is projected to absorb close to a million young professionals a year, roughly a tenth of all new workforce entrants, with India's healthcare staffing market itself growing at a 9.4% CAGR through 2035. Salaries reflect that demand curve too: entry-level allied health roles typically start around Rs. 2-4.5 LPA, with specialisation and hospital-network experience pushing mid-career earnings well past that.

Why Choose Assam down town University for Your Professional Healthcare Studies?

AdtU's Allied & Healthcare Sciences and Physiotherapy & Rehabilitation faculties run Bachelor's and Master's programmes in Anaesthesia& Operation Theatre Technology, Medical Radiology & Imaging Technology, Medical Laboratory Science, Dialysis Therapy Technology, Optometry, Nutrition& Dietetics, and Physiotherapy, alongside Nursing (ANM, GNM, B.Sc., M.Sc.) and Pharmaceutical Sciences (D.Pharm, B.Pharm, M.Pharm) - all healthcare courses in Assam backed by recognition from the UGC, NAAC A+ grade, AICTE, the Indian Nursing Council, the Pharmacy Council of India, and the Indian Association of Physiotherapists. Diploma-level entry after Class 10 or 12 is also available for students who want a shorter, skill-focused route into fields like Medical Laboratory Science or Optometry. On the outcomes side, AdtU's Class of 2025 recorded a highest package of Rs. 15+ LPA, and the 2026 outgoing batch has already logged 900+ placement offers through 150+ recruiters - including healthcare names like Apollo Dialysis, Narayana Health, and Sun Pharma. For students comparing healthcare courses in Guwahati, that combination of statutory recognition and an active placement pipeline is worth weighing alongside the course itself. Admissions details are at apply.adtu.in.



FAQs

1. Can I build a successful healthcare career and work in hospitals without an MBBS degree?

Yes. The demand for these jobs is constantly increasing. India is currently facing a shortage of over 10 lakh allied health professionals. Pharmacists, nurses, physiotherapists, radiographers, lab scientists and dialysis technicians work directly within hospitals and diagnostic centres.

2. Which healthcare courses without NEET offer the best career growth and salary opportunities?

Most obvious NEET-free career option with decent long-term growth remains pharmacy. Most institutions provide nursing without NEET. Allied health professions such as radiology, dialysis therapy and optometry also provide good salary growth but check current entry requirements with the ongoing regulatory changes in 2026-27.

3. Are allied healthcare courses recognized in India and abroad?

Yes. Most obvious NEET-free career option with decent long-term growth remains pharmacy. Most institutions provide nursing without NEET. Allied health professions such as radiology, dialysis therapy and optometry also provide good salary growth but check current entry requirements with the ongoing regulatory changes in 2026-27.

4. Does Assam down town University (AdtU) provide placement and internship opportunities for healthcare students?

Yes. Apart from the clinical and internship exposure integrated into its healthcare programmes, AdtU has a dedicated placement function; the 2026 outgoing batch across the university recorded 900+ placement offers through 150+ recruiters, including healthcare-sector employers.

Programme Overview





M.Sc. in Forensic Science is a 2-year postgraduate programme which deals with applications of basic and advanced study subjects, such as chemistry, biology, physics, computer science, IT geology, psychology, social sciences, etc. to criminal investigations and judicial procedures. Forensic science plays a vital role in modern crime-solving, addressing the rise in complex criminal activities and the increasing reliance of courts on scientific evidence. After completion of this course, students may opt for various higher studies like PhD, which will improve their chances for better jobs.






Programme Educational Objectives





AdtU Forensic Science postgraduates will be equipped for professional careers as forensic experts, consultants, and specialists in law enforcement, legal advisory, and private investigation.
Postgraduates will serve as forensic experts and educators, contributing to a secure, healthy, and vibrant society by raising public awareness of criminal strategies.
Postgraduates will be capable of integrating AI-based tools & techniques with modern forensic technologies for comprehensive evidence detection, analysis, and evaluation.








Programme Outcomes





Forensic Knowledge: Apply advanced principles, theories, and cutting-edge practices of basic sciences to analyze and resolve forensic challenges for the advancement and efficiency of criminal investigation.
Problem Analysis & Solving: Identifying, analyzing, and solving intricate forensic problems using advanced critical thinking, scientific reasoning, and interdisciplinary approaches to draw precise and reliable conclusions.
Investigation and Research: Apply research competency to design hypotheses and experiments using modern tools and techniques, and analyse and interpret the data to arrive at logical conclusions in the area of forensic science.
Communication: Effectively communicate information among the scientific community and society and be able to prepare documents and reports, and deliver impactful presentations.
Professional Ethics: Comply to the highest ethical standards in all forensic practices, ensuring integrity, impartiality, and confidentiality while upholding legal, moral, and ethical guidelines in their professional conduct.
Environment and Sustainability: Understand and evaluate the environmental impact of forensic activities, striving to balance scientific goals with ecological preservation and sustainability.
Individual and Teamwork: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings to maintain highest standards of professionalism and integrity.
Case management: Able to engage in lifelong learning and active engagement with the scientific and professional communities in the broadest context of scientific and technological advancement.








Programme Specific Outcomes





Experiential Learning: Integrate forensic science expertise for impactful and sustainable solutions for communities.
Innovation and Entrepreneurship: Design and develop innovative forensic tools, investigative kits, software, sensors, fingerprint powders, and other advanced solutions to address emerging challenges in the field.
Investigative Partnership: Collaborate with local investigating agencies applying forensic techniques to address crimes at the regional and local levels, contributing to effective investigations and justice in the community.













Eligibility :Bachelor's degree in Life Science, Applied Science, Forensic Science, Medicine, Engineering, Pharmacy, Dentistry, or Ayush, with a minimum of 50% aggregate from any government or private University.

Eligibility

Programme Overview





B.Sc. in Forensic Science is a 4-year undergraduate programme under Faculty of Science of Assam downtown University, Guwahati, Assam. The main aim of the Programme is to create experts in the field of forensic science with the application of advanced scientific techniques This course targets to develop a platform where students can get to learn and practice about the scientific methodology and techniques that can be used to the field of crime investigation so that justice can be serve to the right person in less time which is the need of the hour for society. A graduate in forensic science course may avail jobs in the Forensic science laboratories, Research and Development, Education, Armed forces and Private sector also.






Programme Educational Objectives





AdtU forensic science graduates will be well-prepared for successful careers ni industry, corporate, research organizations and/ or government sectors in one or more of the disciplines/ sub-disciplines of forensic science.
The forensic graduates will be academically prepared to apply advanced technologies for analyzing forensic evidence, leading diverse teams and delivering impartial scientific opinions.
AdtU forensic graduates will play a vital role in fostering a safe and vibrant society by serving as forensic experts for crime awareness, with the potential for successful pursuits in higher education in forensic science fi pursued.








Programme Outcomes





Apply fundamental concepts of basic and applied sciences, criminal laws aspects, forensic sciences principles and analytical processes with psycho-social aspects in investigation to support the agencies and the criminal justice system.
Examine physical evidence, witness statements, and forensic findings to understand the sequence of evidence, addressing intricate forensic challenges and formulating logical procedural approaches.
Identify and analyze complex forensic problems using standard analytical protocols and methods.
Identify, formulate and analyze forensic problems utilizing evidence- based research to draw logical conclusions.
Communicate efficiently with individuals, peers, investigating agencies and other stakeholders, and prepare quality reports to convey findings.
Adhere to the code of conduct and ethical values in the profession.
Perform efficiently as a member or leader in collaboration with multidisciplinary teams and diverse settings.
Recognize and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern scientific theories with an understanding of scientific principles.
Engage in lifelong learning staying abreast of advancements in forensic technology and practices.








Programme Specific Outcomes





Apply the comprehensive understanding of multidisciplinary concepts of forensic science with interdisciplinary approaches to address complex forensic problems.
Foster interpersonal ability and adaptability in diverse socio- cultural teams for efficient working in the profession through co-curricular and extra-curricular activities.
Ability to address forensic issues and understand international scenarios through global certification courses.













Eligibility :Passed 10+2 (or its equivalent) in Science with subjects including Physics, Chemistry, Biology, or Mathematics, with a minimum of 50% aggregate.






Curriculum Details
Year wise Course Details








Year 1

















Odd Semester

Courses for this
semester









CRIME SCENE MANAGEMENT



Course Overview

1. Comprehend crime scene definition, importance, management, and reasons for crimes in India.
2. Recognize various crime scene types and roles of police, experts, and judicial officers.
3. Learn barricading, photography, sketching, and search techniques for indoor and outdoor crime scenes.
4. Understand types, collection, preservation, and chain of custody for physical evidence.
5. Grasp principles and stages of crime scene reconstruction, from data collection to theory formulation.

Course Outcomes






Recognize crime scene investigation, and understand the reasons for crime along with their practical aspects



Explain different crime scene types and comprehend the role of investigating agencies in crime scene management along with their practical aspects



Apply techniques for documenting crime scenes, utilizing various search patterns along with their practical aspects



DiDescribe the methods for collecting evidences, package, and preserve, and maintain the chain of custody for crime exhibits along with their practical aspects



Analyze crime scene reconstruction using various principles of data collection, hypothesis formulation, testing, and theory formation.










INDIAN CONSTITUTION & LEGAL SYSTEM



Course Overview

1. Grasp offence forms, case classification, legislation components, judicial hierarchy.
2. Differentiate cognizable and non-cognizable offences, bailable and non-bailable offences.
3. Examine Sections related to offences against individuals and property.
4. Explore constitutional articles and legal acts.
5. Dive into specific legal areas and acts' intricacies
Course Outcomes






Define offenses and their forms, compare and distinguish civil and criminal classifications along with their practical aspects in real cases.



Interpret offenses against persons and property, including sexual offenses under relevant sections along with their practical aspects in real cases.



Apply knowledge of evidence and rules of relevancy, including the examination of witnesses and expert testimony



Demonstrate an understanding of constitutional articles and acts, such as the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act along with their practical aspects in real cases.



Interpret various acts, including the Explosive Substances Act, Arms Act, Dowry Prohibition Act, and Wildlife Protection Act along with their practical aspects in real cases










CRIME AND SOCIETY



Course Overview

1. Understand the definition, history, and scope of forensic science.
2. Learn the basic principles, tools, and techniques used in forensic science.
3. Comprehend the elements, characteristics, and causes of crime, and identify different types of criminal behavior.
4. Explore criminological theories and understand the goals and objectives of criminology.
5. Familiarize with various crime investigation agencies in India and their functions
Course Outcomes






Describe history, scope and fundamentals of forensic science, including ethics.



Explain the forensic principles, lab hierarchy, and utilizing forensic tools



Recognize crime elements, deviant behavior, hate crimes, and societal implications along with their practical aspects in real life criminal cases.



Discuss various crime theories, investigative techniques, criminal profiling, and media's impact on criminal cases along with the practical aspects.



Explain India's crime investigating agencies, their roles, and contributions to the criminal justice system










EXTRA-CURRICULAR



Course Overview

Ascertain physical and mental development of the students and select best performers for state, national and international level competition.
Course Outcomes






Identify and describe various sports, music, and co-curricular activities available at the university, and explain the benefits of participating in these activities.



Apply skills and techniques learned in workshops and club activities to participate effectively in sports, music, and other co-curricular competitions, and analyze their performance to identify areas of improvement.



Discuss the reflective essay or presentation assessing how involvement in various activities has contributed to their personal and professional growth, and design a plan for future engagement and skill development.










CHEMISTRY- I



Course Overview

1. Understand the principles of hybridization, shapes of molecules, and chemical bonds, including van der Waals interactions, hydrogen bonding, and electronic displacements in covalent bonds.
2. Explore isomerism concepts, including optical isomerism, geometric isomerism, and conformational isomerism, and understand the nomenclature and properties associated with different isomers.
3. Grasp the kinetic molecular theory of gases, deviations from ideal behavior, and the van der Waals equation, as well as the principles governing the liquefaction of gases.
4. Comprehend the quantum mechanical aspects of atomic structure, including Bohr's theory, wave mechanics, quantum numbers, and the electronic configuration of atoms.
5. Study periodic properties of elements, focusing on effective nuclear charge, atomic radii, ionization enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, and electronegativity, along with their variations in the periodic table.
Course Outcomes






Understand the hybridization of carbon, types of bonds, electronic effects, and the shapes of molecules



Identify the kinetic molecular theory of gases, deviations from ideal behavior, and properties of enantiomers



Explain Bohr’s theory, wave mechanics, and quantum numbers



Understand the periodic properties of elements, including effective nuclear charge and ionization enthalpy



Describe electron gain enthalpy, trends in electronegativity, and the variation of electronegativity with bond order










PHYSICS-I



Course Overview

1. Understand scalar and vector quantities, their properties, and interpretations, including scalar and vector products.
2. Explore coordinate systems, motion concepts, frames of reference, and principles of relativity.
3. Analyze fluid dynamics, elastic properties of matter, and equations like Bernoulli's and continuity.
4. Grasp energy principles, work, conservation, rotational dynamics, and relationships between linear and angular variables.
5. Differentiate wave types, calculate properties, delve into sound waves, and explore ultrasonic applications.
Course Outcomes






Understand scalar and vector properties, coordinate systems, divergence, curl, and the distinction between conservative and non-conservative forces



Identify the concepts of frame of reference, inertial and non-inertial frames, special theory of relativity, Lorentz transformations, and relativistic addition of velocities



Explain the fundamentals of motion, acceleration, projectile motion, pseudo forces, elastic properties of matter, fluid dynamics, and equations like Bernoulli’s



Explain the concepts of energy, kinetic energy, work, rotational variables, and the conservation of energy, especially in rotational motion



Describe different types of waves, sound waves, Doppler effect, sound intensity measurement, and the introduction to ultrasonic waves and their applications










BIOLOGY- I



Course Overview

1. Develop a comprehensive understanding of Algae, covering general characteristics, classification, reproduction, and economic significance.
2. Study the fundamental aspects of fungi, including their characteristics, classification, and economic importance.
3. Explore lichens, understanding their general features, structure, reproduction, and economic importance.
4. Gain insights into Bryophytes, covering characteristics, classification, reproduction, and economic relevance
5. Examine Pteridophytes, focusing on characteristics, classification, reproduction, and economic importance. Additionally, explore ecological concepts such as ecosystems, energy flow, biogeochemical cycles, and succession.

Course Outcomes






Understand the general characteristics, classification, modes of reproduction, and economic significance of algae



Identify the general features, classification of fungi, and their economic importance



Understand of the general aspects, structure, reproduction, and economic significance of lichens



Identify the general characteristics, classification, modes of reproduction, and economic importance of bryophytes



Identify the concept of ecosystems, their structure and function, energy flow, biogeochemical cycles, and the process of succession

FORENSIC PHYSICS



Course Overview

1. Understand and apply principles of impression evidence analysis, including tyre marks, skid marks, serial number restoration, and vehicular accident assessment.
2. Identify, classify, and analyze tool marks, emphasizing class and individual characteristics, tracing, lifting, and photographic examination.
3. Examine glass properties, including composition, fractures, and direction of impact, and conduct soil examinations based on color, density, size distribution, and chemical analysis.
4. Identify types of paints, conduct microscopic and macroscopic studies, analyze pigment distribution, and perform pyrolysis gas chromatography.
5. Understand hair structure, collection, and evaluation, and classify fibers, conducting microscopic, physical, chemical, and instrumental examinations
Course Outcomes






Identify and analyze various impression evidence types in the context of forensic investigations



Apply techniques for making casts, and obliteration and restoration methods, showcasing competence in tool mark analysis.



Demonstrate expertise in glass and soil analysis, contributing to forensic investigations through comprehensive examinations along with their practical aspects.



Exhibit proficiency in forensic paint examinations, including physical matching and chemical analyses.



Demonstrate competence in hair and fiber analysis, providing valuable contributions to forensic investigations involving these types of physical evidence along with their practical aspects










FINGERPRINTS & OTHER IMPRESSIONS



Course Overview

1. Understand the historical development and biological foundation of fingerprints.
2. Analyze and interpret fingerprint patterns, ridge characters, and minutiae.
3. Explore the classification and cataloging of fingerprint records, including the use of automated systems.
4. Investigate the constituents of sweat residue and employ various methods for latent fingerprint detection.
5. Investigate the constituents of sweat residue and employ various methods for latent fingerprint detection
Course Outcomes






Understanding the historical facts and basic concepts of fingerprinting.



Analyze various fingerprint patterns, including ridge characters/minutiae, and differentiate types fingerprints found at crime scenes along with their practical aspects



Explain classification and cataloging of fingerprint records, including automated systems, and understand the significance of poroscopy and edgeoscopy along with their practical aspects



Analyze and interpret latent fingerprints through physical and chemical methods, preservation, and lifting, including digital imaging techniques along with their practical aspects



Illustrate the importance of footprints casting techniques, electrostatic lifting of latent footprints, and understand the historical significance of palm prints and lip prints along with their practical aspects










CHEMISTRY- 2



Course Overview

1. Understand the principles of isomerism, including its sources, methods of formation, and physical and chemical properties of alkanes, alkenes, and alkynes, along with mechanisms involved.
2. Explore the formation and chemical reactions of alkyl halides and aryl halides, emphasizing nucleophilic substitution reactions and their mechanisms.
3. Examine irreversible and reversible reactions, chemical equilibrium, the law of mass action, and the thermodynamic treatment of the law of mass action.
4. Gain insights into various types of chemical bonds, oxidation numbers, and theories such as Lewis theory, Valence Bond theory, and Molecular Orbital theory.
5. Understand acid-base reactions through the Brönsted-Lowry concept, solvated proton, levelling solvents, Lewis acid-base concept, and the application of Hard and Soft Acids and Bases (HSAB) principle.
Course Outcomes






Understand the diverse isomerism and mastering the physical and chemical properties of alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and aromatic compound



Interpret in handling the methods of formation, reactions, and mechanisms involved in alkyl and aryl halides.



Explain chemical equilibrium principles, Le Chatelier's principle, and their applications.



Identify chemical bonding, structure, and hybridization principles in the context of molecular orbitals



Describe application of acid-base concepts, including Brönsted-Lowry, Lewis theories, and the Hard and Soft Acids and Bases (HSAB) principle










PHYSICS- 2



Course Overview

1. Grasp electric fields, Gauss' Law, and conservative nature of electrostatics.
2. Understand polarization, dielectric effects, and electric displacement in matter.
3. Define magnetic fields, calculate forces, and explore magnetic interactions.
4. Study magnetization, susceptibility, and ferromagnetism in materials.
5. Investigate electromagnetic induction, Maxwell's Equations, and circuit phenomena like resonance.
Course Outcomes






Classify fundamental electrostatic concepts, including electric field, Gauss’ Law, and capacitance, applying them to charge distributions of varying symmetry



Understand electric fields in matter, polarization, and dielectric properties, effectively employing Gauss’ Law in dielectrics



Understand and apply magnetic forces, Biot-Savart’s Law, Ampere’s Circuital Law, and properties of the magnetic field to calculate forces and torques in current-carrying systems



Explain magnetization, magnetic intensity, susceptibility, and permeability, exploring ferromagnetism and understanding the B-H curve and hysteresis



Demonstrate proficiency in electromagnetic induction principles, including Faraday’s Law, Lenz’s Law, and an introduction to Maxwell’s Equations, applying them to AC circuits, resonance, and power dissipation










BIOLOGY- 2



Course Overview

1. Introduce principles and basis for animal classification.
2. Explore general characters, classification, and life histories of major animal phyla.
3. Introduce protochordates and agnatha, highlighting general features and significance in vertebrate evolution
4. Cover general features and classification of fishes, amphibians, and reptiles
5. Introduce general features and classification of birds and mammals.
Course Outcomes






Enable comprehension of the rationale behind animal kingdom classification in biological sciences



Understand the diverse animal phyla, their characteristics, and evolutionary significance



Understand protochordates and agnatha characteristics and their role in vertebrate evolution



Identify aquatic adaptations, parental care, and classifications in aquatic vertebrates.



Demonstration of flight adaptations, adaptive radiation, and locomotory appendages in birds and mammals

DNA FORENSIC



Course Overview

1. Introduce students to DNA as the biological blueprint and methods for DNA extraction and quantitation in forensic analysis.

2. Explore the medico-legal aspects of death, including the diagnosis, stages, and signs of death, as well as different types of fatal incidents.
3. Provide knowledge on the autopsy process, including internal and external
examinations, sample collection, and the investigation of sexual offences and suicidal cases.
4. Educate students on the types and classification of injuries, including antemortem and post-mortem injuries, and specific injury types like bite marks and burn injuries.

Conduct thorough autopsies, including internal and external examinations, sample collection, and the investigation of specific cases like sexual offences and suicides

Apply forensic entomology techniques to estimate the time since death and understand the decomposition process










WILDLIFE AND ENVIRONMENTAL FORENSIC



Course Overview

1) Understand the fundamental concepts of wildlife, protected species, and endangered species, and develop skills in the identification of wildlife materials.
2. Apply knowledge of pug mark identification, wildlife population censuses, and forensic necropsy, and comprehend the legal aspects of wildlife protection.
3. Gain proficiency in forensic entomology, including the identification of insects, collection of entomological evidence, and understanding insect succession in forensic investigations
Course Outcomes





Demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of the importance of wildlife, protected and endangered species, and proficiency in identifying wildlife materials through conventional and modern methods.



Apply knowledge in the identification of pug marks, conducting wildlife population censuses, and performing forensic necropsy, while understanding the legal frameworks like the Wildlife Protection Act and Environment Protection Act.



Exhibit a foundational understanding of forensic entomology, recognizing insects of forensic importance, collecting entomological evidence in death investigations, and applying insect succession to determine the time since death



Analyze various botanical evidence of forensic significance, including leaves and seeds, and demonstrate the isolation and forensic importance of diatoms



Evaluate environmental standards for air, water, and noise quality, and demonstrate knowledge of environmental laws, policies, protection agencies, waste treatment methods, and biodegradation processes

FORENSIC TOXICOLOGY



Course Overview

1. Introduce students to poison classification, signs of drug addiction, drug toxicity, and methods for extracting poisons from biological specimens.
2. Explore pharmacology and toxicology of psychotropic drugs, including sedatives, stimulants, opiates, and drugs of abuse.
3. Cover the nature, administration, signs, symptoms, and detection of corrosive poisons, arsenic, mercury, and lead.
4. Explore pesticides, their isolation, detection, and estimation, as well as volatile poisons like methyl alcohol and chloroform.
5. Introduce students to animal and plant poisons, blood alcohol analysis, breath test
instruments, and asphyxiants like cyanide and carbon monoxide.

Course Outcomes





Understand the foundational knowledge and practical skills to identify and analyze toxic
substances in forensic contexts along with their practical aspects.



Explain the effects of psychotropic drugs and their implications in forensic investigations along
with their practical aspects



Interpret metallic poison analysis and their medico-legal aspects.



Analyze non-volatile and volatile poisons, understanding their effects and contributing to forensic investigations along with their practical aspects.



Analyze miscellaneous poisons contributing to forensic examination in complex and rare cases










FORENSIC ANTHROPOLOGY



Course Overview

1. Understand the definition, scope, and application of Forensic Anthropology, with a focus on the study of the human skeleton.
2. Learn the nature, formation, and methods for identification of human bones, with an emphasis on estimating age, race, sex, and stature from skeletal material.
3. Explore the importance and necessity of personal identification in forensic anthropology, particularly in cases requiring personal identification.
4. Master Somatoscopy, focusing on the observation of various anatomical features and marks for personal identification purposes.
5. Acquire knowledge of Somatometry and indices for measurements of different body parts,
along with the study of burned bones and bone fragments in mass disasters.
Course Outcomes





Identify human skeleton for estimation of age, race, sex, and stature along with their practical
aspects



Apply personal identification techniques, including somatoscopy, for observing and recording
anatomical features, scars, occupational marks, and tattoos along with their practical aspects.



Illustrate Somatometry measurements and interpret indices for various body parts, contributing
to personal identification in forensic scenarios along with their practical aspects



Analyze burned bones and bone fragments in mass disasters



Utilize facial reconstruction techniques

Programme Overview





Physical Education is one of the most effective forms of education, delivered through physical exercises, recreational activities, and sports. As an integral part of the educational process, it promotes holistic development by fostering immediate and long-term benefits. Participation in physical activities and sports strengthens muscles and bones, enhances energy levels, improves coordination, and significantly reduces the risk of chronic diseases. This applies to individuals across all age groups—children, adults, and the elderly—who enjoy and benefit from active lifestyles.
The curriculum framework for the Bachelor of Physical Education and Sports (B.P.E.S.) Honors 3-year undergraduate program is designed to provide a comprehensive structure within the field of Physical Education. Developed in alignment with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, it caters to the diverse needs of students while ensuring a standardized and high-quality Physical Education degree across the country.
The framework also facilitates periodic program reviews to maintain relevance and quality, ensuring students are equipped with the skills and knowledge to thrive in the field of Physical Education and sports.






Programme Educational Objectives





Skill and Knowledge Development:
Equip students with refined motor skills, scientific understanding of the body’s responses to exercise, and expertise in diverse sports training methods to excel in physical activities and sports science.
Holistic Growth and Professional Competence:
Foster comprehensive physical, mental, and social development, cultivate positive attitudes toward sports, and prepare students for roles in officiating, organizing, and managing sports professionally.
Health Advocacy and Integration:
Promote lifelong health and well-being, encourage healthy habits, and facilitate social integration through the principles of physical education and sports.








Programme Outcomes





Skill Development: Refining motor skills and enhancing proficiency in physical activities.
Scientific Knowledge: Understanding the body’s response to various exercises and the principles of sports science.
Health and Fitness: Promoting fitness and overall well-being.
Positive Attitudes: Cultivating a positive mindset toward physical activity and sports.
Holistic Growth: Encouraging comprehensive development through sports and physical education.
Officiating Skills: Gaining knowledge of rules and regulations for effective officiating in sports.
Organizational Abilities: Building expertise in organizing sports and games professionally.
Allied Knowledge: Applying scientific principles from allied disciplines in sports and physical education.
Sports Training: Understanding diverse methods and strategies for effective sports training.
Health and Social Integration: Promoting healthy habits and fostering social integration among athletes.








Programme Specific Outcomes





Comprehensive Skill and Knowledge Development:
Graduates will acquire advanced motor skills, scientific understanding of exercise physiology, and expertise in diverse sports training methods to excel in physical education and sports science.
Professional Competence in Sports Management:
Graduates will demonstrate the ability to effectively officiate, organize, and manage sports events and activities, adhering to rules and professional standards.
Health Promotion and Social Integration: Graduates will promote lifelong health and well-being, foster positive attitudes, and encourage social cohesion through active participation in sports and physical education.

Programme Overview





The Master of Optometry (M. Optom) is a postgraduate program designed to offer comprehensive knowledge and advanced clinical skills in the field of optometry. Throughout the curriculum, students delve into subjects such as advanced ocular diagnostics, therapeutic interventions, contact lenses, low vision rehabilitation, and binocular vision. Practical experience is gained through clinical rotations in diverse eye care settings, providing hands-on learning opportunities. Additionally, research components are integrated into the program, enabling students to contribute to the advancement of the field. Ultimately, the program aims to equip optometrists with specialized expertise, fostering a thorough understanding of eye care and preparing them for specialized roles within the industry.






Programme Educational Objectives





Advanced Clinical and Professional Practice: Graduates will establish themselves as advanced optometry professionals by delivering evidence-based, ethical, patient-centered, and specialty eye care while demonstrating leadership and interprofessional collaboration in diverse healthcare settings.
Research, Innovation and Academic Excellence: Graduates will contribute to the advancement of optometry through high-quality research, innovation, teaching, scholarly activities, and the application of emerging technologies to improve clinical practice and education.
Leadership and Community Engagement: Graduates will promote equitable eye care by leading community eye health initiatives, influencing healthcare policies, advocating for the profession, and engaging in lifelong learning and continuous professional development.








Programme Outcomes





Advanced Clinical Competence: Demonstrate advanced competency in the diagnosis, clinical decision-making, management, and co-management of complex ocular and visual disorders using contemporary diagnostic technologies and evidence-based clinical practice.
Specialty Optometric Practice: Apply specialized knowledge and advanced clinical skills in areas such as contact lenses, low vision rehabilitation, vision therapy, ocular surface disorders, myopia management, and advanced anterior and posterior segment care.
Research and Scientific Scholarship: Design, conduct, analyze, interpret, and disseminate high-quality research by applying scientific methods, biostatistics, critical appraisal, and evidence-based practice to address clinical and public health challenges in optometry.
Community Eye Health and Public Health Leadership: Develop, implement, and evaluate community eye health programmes, epidemiological studies, preventive eye care strategies, and innovative public health interventions to improve population eye health.
Professionalism, Ethics and Leadership: Demonstrate ethical practice, professional accountability, leadership, multidisciplinary collaboration, quality assurance, and effective healthcare management while promoting excellence in patient care and professional practice.
Teaching, Mentoring and Academic Excellence: Design curriculum, formulate learning outcomes, implement learner-centered teaching strategies, conduct competency-based assessments, provide constructive feedback, and mentor undergraduate learners using evidence-based educational practices.
Innovation and Technology: Utilize emerging diagnostic technologies, digital health solutions, artificial intelligence, and innovative clinical approaches to enhance patient care, research, education, and healthcare delivery.
Lifelong Learning and Professional Development: Engage in continuous professional development through self-directed learning, critical evaluation of scientific literature, reflective practice, research, and adoption of emerging knowledge and technologies to advance optometry practice and education.
Advocacy and Policy Development: Demonstrate the ability to advocate for vision and eye health, contribute to healthcare policy development, promote equitable and accessible eye care services, and actively participate in professional organizations to advance the optometry profession and improve population eye health.








Programme Specific Outcomes





Advanced Clinical Competency: Demonstrate expertise in comprehensive and specialty optometric practice by integrating advanced diagnostic techniques, evidence-based clinical decision-making, therapeutic management, rehabilitation, and multidisciplinary patient care for complex ocular and visual disorders.
Research, Education and Innovation: Design and conduct independent research, critically evaluate scientific evidence, disseminate research findings, implement competency-based teaching-learning strategies, and utilize emerging technologies, including digital health and artificial intelligence, to advance optometric practice and education.
Leadership, Public Health and Professional Advancement: Plan, implement, and evaluate community eye health programmes, lead quality improvement initiatives, advocate for accessible and equitable vision care, uphold ethical and professional standards, and contribute to healthcare policy and the advancement of the optometry profession.













Eligibility :Bachelor of Optometry (B. Optom) on regular mode from recognised university






Curriculum Details
Year wise Course Details








Year 1

















Odd Semester

Courses for this
semester









APPLIED OPTOMETRIC OPTICS



Course Overview

This course deals with the application of the optical properties of light , the eye as a visual system and advanced dispensing techniques.
Course Outcomes





Apply theoretical knowledge in a clinical setting, performing comprehensive eye examinations and prescribing corrective lenses based on individual patient needs.



Understanding the optical principle.



Differentiate between lens materials, designs, and coatings.



Advanced optical technologies.



Analyze and interpret prescription information.










OCULAR DISEASE AND DIAGNOSTIC



Course Overview

This course covers the principles and applications of ophthalmic instrumentation, providing students with essential skills for accurate ocular investigations, proficiency in advanced instruments, and adherence to quality assurance and safety standards in ophthalmology.
Course Outcomes





Develop advanced diagnostic skills for identifying ocular diseases.



Participants will acquire essential skills in conducting ocular investigations, ensuring accurate diagnosis and patient management.



Proficiency in utilizing advanced ophthalmic instruments such as corneal topographers, imaging devices, and electrophysiological tools will be achieved.



Students will develop competence in the use of surgical instrumentation, contributing to effective participation in ophthalmic surgical procedures.



Upon completion, participants will adhere to quality assurance and safety standards, fostering ethical and responsible practices in the field of ophthalmology.










PUBLIC HEALTH & COMMUNITY OPTOMETRY



Course Overview

This course explores the intersection of public health and optometry, covering foundational principles, epidemiological applications, community-based eye care program development, effective health education, and advocacy for optometric services within legal and ethical frameworks.
Course Outcomes





Examine the foundational principles of public health to identify their relevance and application within the field of optometry.



Apply epidemiological methods to analyze the prevalence, incidence, and risk factors of eye-related conditions in diverse populations.



Create and implement community-based eye care programs, integrating evidence-based strategies to address specific needs within different communities.



Develop effective communication skills and employ behavioral change models, ensuring culturally competent health education in optometric practice.



Discuss about the components of health economy and the role of Third Party Administrators (TPA).











Show More













Even Semester

Courses for this
semester









ADVANCED CONTACT LENS - I



Course Overview

An advanced contact lens course in an optometry syllabus is designed to provide optometry students with specialized knowledge and skills related to the fitting, prescribing, and management of contact lenses. The course aims to equip students with a deep understanding of advanced contact lens concepts, technologies, and clinical applications.
Course Outcomes





Understand ocular anatomy and physiology.



Explore the latest advancements in contact lens materials, including silicone hydrogels, hybrid lenses, and other specialty materials.



Develop skills in using advanced diagnostic tools for assessing corneal curvature, tear film quality, and other factors crucial for precise contact lens fitting.



Understand fitting technique and problem solving.



Understand and implement of the push-up test and Taco method in the fitting and assessment of soft contact lenses.










LOW VISION & GERIATRIC OPTOMETRY - I



Course Overview

This course focuses on the assessment and management of low vision in the geriatric population. It covers various eye conditions associated with aging, strategies for optimizing visual function, and the use of low-vision aids. Practical skills in conducting assessments and developing appropriate interventions will be emphasized.
Course Outcomes





Understand the epidemiology and demographics of visual impairment in the elderly population.



Understand about low vision rehabilitation.



Demonstrate knowledge of the physiological changes in the aging eye and their impact on visual function.



Perform comprehensive eye examinations for geriatric patients, incorporating specialized assessment techniques.



Utilize diagnostic tools and technologies for accurate assessment of low vision in elderly individuals.










APPLIED CLINICAL OPTOMETRY



Course Overview

Students will be able to conduct a comprehensive eye examination, incorporating assessments of visual acuity, refraction, ocular health, and relevant diagnostic tests.
Course Outcomes





Develop proficiency in conducting comprehensive eye examinations.



Gain hands-on experience using diagnostic tools and instruments.



Acquire the ability to diagnose common eye conditions and vision problems.



Understand the principles of refraction and prescribing corrective lenses.



Demonstrate ophthalmoscopy and its applications in the assessment of the fundus.










PEDIATRIC OPTOMETRY & BINOCULAR VISION- I



Course Overview

A comprehensive course in pediatric optometry and binocular vision covers the assessment, diagnosis, and management of pediatric eye conditions, along with the principles of binocular vision, to equip students with the knowledge and skills needed for effective clinical practice.
Course Outcomes





Students will demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of normal visual development in children and the factors influencing pediatric eye health.



Students will be able to proficiently conduct a pediatric eye examination, including an accurate assessment of visual acuity, refractive errors, and binocular vision function.



Students will demonstrate a solid understanding of the principles of binocular vision, including convergence, accommodation, and sensory fusion.



Students will recognize and diagnose binocular vision disorders such as amblyopia and strabismus, and develop comprehensive treatment strategies.



Student will learn about vision therapy using in pediatric patient.










OCULAR DISEASES & THERAPEUTICS



Course Overview

The course provides a comprehensive exploration of ocular anatomy, diseases, and therapeutic interventions, equipping students with the knowledge, diagnostic skills, and clinical competencies necessary for understanding and managing a wide range of ocular conditions.
Course Outcomes





Students should demonstrate a comprehensive understanding of ocular anatomy, physiology, and the pathophysiology of various ocular diseases.



Students should be proficient in using diagnostic tools such as slit-lamp examination, tonometry, and imaging modalities for accurate assessment and diagnosis.



Develop clinical competence in performing basic ophthalmic procedures, examinations, and history-taking, demonstrating proficiency in a clinical setting.



Apply knowledge of various treatment modalities, including medical, surgical, and laser interventions, in the management of ocular diseases.



Students will learn about apply evidence-based approaches to treatment planning and patient care.

Courses for this
semester









ADVANCED CONTACT LENS II



Course Overview

The advanced contact lens course in optometry provides comprehensive instruction and hands-on experience in the fitting, assessment, and management of various contact lenses, including specialty lenses, to equip students with the knowledge and skills necessary for advanced clinical practice in optometry.
Course Outcomes





Demonstrate knowledge of specialty contact lenses for conditions such as keratoconus, irregular corneas, and post-surgical needs.



Develop proficiency in fitting various types of contact lenses, including rigid gas permeable, soft, toric, and multifocal lenses.



Master the techniques for assessing lens fit, centration, and movement.



Gain experience in troubleshooting and problem-solving for common contact lens complications.



Stay current with emerging technologies in contact lens design, materials, and smart/contact lenses with drug-delivery capabilities.










LOW VISION & GERIATRIC OPTOMETRY II



Course Overview

This course is designed to provide advanced knowledge and practical skills in the field of Low Vision and Geriatric Optometry. It will cover the assessment, management, and rehabilitation of visual impairments in older adults, with a focus on optimizing visual function and quality of life.
Course Outcomes





Understand the aging process.



Student will learn to perform comprehensive geriatric eye examination.



Student will learn to asses and manage low vision.



Apply optical and non-optical strategies to improve visual function in geriatric patients.



Evaluate the effectiveness of different low vision interventions.










PEDIATRIC OPTOMETRY & BINOCULAR VISION II



Course Overview

Advanced Pediatric Optometry & Binocular Vision course focuses on equipping students with the specialized knowledge and skills necessary to provide comprehensive eye care for pediatric patients, covering developmental aspects, binocular vision disorders, refractive errors, contact lens fitting, and the integration of advanced technologies in pediatric optometry.

Comprehensive understanding of pediatric eye care.



Proficiency in binocular vision assessment.



Ability to manage pediatric ocular pathology.



Student will learn about integration of technology in pediatric optometry.



Student will learn about special clinical condition like motor disability.

By exploring theoretical frameworks alongside hands-on experiences, students develop the knowledge, skills, and dispositions necessary for fostering meaningful learning experiences and promoting student success.
Course Outcomes





Utilize effective teaching strategies to engage learners and facilitate understanding.



Demonstrate the ability to assess learner comprehension and adjust teaching methods accordingly.



Explore theories of adult learning and their application in teaching ocular disease and therapeutics.



Develop proficiency in delivering educational content related to ocular disease and therapeutics.



Develop skills in assessing learner comprehension and providing constructive feedback.

Master of Science in Zoology

2 Years Master Degree Programme


















Our Approach







Global Education, Global Acceptance




The course is designed to acquire adequate knowledge of biodiversity and the anatomy of animals

Addresses the causes of loss of habitat, disease and effect of climate change on animal life.

The curriculum includes lectures, seminars, report writing reports and essays, field trips, interaction sessions with industry speakers, project and research

Excellent placement records which include both private and public sectors

Special thrust in research and project work

Programme Details









2 Years Programme

Programme Overview





The Zoology program equips graduates for careers in industry, agriculture, and research. They develop professional, communication, and ethical skills, blending innovation and entrepreneurship for personal and national growth, while remaining responsive to societal needs and committed to lifelong learning. Graduates will identify and analyze biotechnological problems, apply multidisciplinary concepts, and achieve global competency. They gain scientific knowledge, laboratory and analytical skills, and problem-solving abilities in various fields. Proficiency in scientific tools, enhanced communication skills, adherence to professional ethics, and a research-oriented mindset are emphasized. Social and environmental responsibility, promoting sustainability, and contributing to societal development are key outcomes.






Programme Educational Objectives





Graduates will apply the theoretical knowledge gained during the program to actual practice of laboratory animal science.
Graduates will develop problem solving skills in students and encourage them to carry out innovative research projects thereby enkindling in them the spirit of knowledge creation.
Graduates will be equipped to perform functions that demand higher competence in national/ international organizations, education sectors and NGO’s.
Graduates will serve the community by providing skilled on Apiculture and Ornamental Fish.








Programme Outcomes





Disciplinary Knowledge: Apply comprehensive knowledge of basic sciences, biostatistics, life sciences and specialization in zoological sciences for solving complex health, agricultural, taxonomical and ecological issues.
Problem Solving: Identify, review research literature, formulate, analyse and evaluate complex zoological problems using critical thinking.
Reasoning and Research: Recognise the cause and effect, design hypothesis and experiments using modern tools and techniques, analyse and interpret the data to draw reasonable conclusions.
Communication: Communicate efficiently among stakeholders and society at large, and being able to write documents/scientific reports and deliver effective presentations.
Values and Ethics: Comply with human values and ethics and its strict application in the profession.
Environmental Sustainability: Understand the impact of the formulated solutions in socio-environmental context and redesign considering sustainable global development.
Teamwork: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.
Lifelong Learning: Ability to engage in independent lifelong learning in the broadest context of scientific advancement.








Programme Specific Outcomes





Proficiency in scientific knowledge and career prospects: Apply the skills and empowerment necessary to address challenges within the domains of zoology and it opens up a multitude of employment opportunities in the relevant field with special emphasise to global certification courses.
Critical Thinking: Able to promote a multidisciplinary approach for research exploration and collaboration with professionals across diverse disciplines.
Techno-Professional Skill Development: Should have the capability to cultivate ethical values in the practice of professionalism, emphasizing integrity, responsibility, continuous learning, and skill refinement in alignment with the latest advancements in zoological science.













Eligibility :45% in B.Sc. or any equivalent degree






Curriculum Details
Year wise Course Details








Year 1

















Odd Semester

Courses for this
semester









TAXONOMY AND BASIC ENTOMOLOGY



Course Overview

1. To impart the knowledge of taxonomy and schools of biological classification.
2. To provide the knowledge of application of zoology in insect pest management.
3. To provide skill on insect- based industries for the benefit of mankind.

Course Outcomes






Discuss the history and concept of taxonomy and its classification



Identify various approaches of taxonomy and its importance



Describe the collection, identification and preservation process of animal



Identify insect pests and vectors responsible for diseases



Determine the commercial value of insects and plan for rearing insects










GENETICS



Course Overview

1. To introduce learner to the science of heredity, from its basic principles to the most recent advances in the field.
2. To impart knowledge on genetic alterations in human genome, classical and molecular genetics.
3. To impart knowledge on classical and molecular genetics.

Course Outcomes






Describe chromatin, chromosomes, heterochromatin and euchromatin.



Explain mechanisms of sex determination, dosage compensation in human, Drosophila, and C. Elegans, discuss on structural and numerical aberrations of chromosomes.



Apply karyotyping and pedigree method for identification of inheritance patterns in genetic disorders, use logarithm of the odds scores for linkage testing in specific disease contexts.



Evaluate polygenic inheritance, heritability through Quantitative Trait Locus mapping, linkage maps, and tetrad analysis, explain Human Genome Project and Mapping.



Discuss lac and tryptophan operon concept of gene regulation, in prokaryotes, gene regulation in eukaryotes, explain restrictive enzymes and their role in recombinant DNA techniques.










BIOCHEMISTRY AND BIOINSTRUMENTATION



Course Overview

• To understand the fundamentals of structure, composition and function of biomolecules. To develop knowledge and identify the chemical logic of bioenergetics and metabolic pathways.
• To impart knowledge of principles and applications of analytical instruments in life sciences.
• To analyze biological samples for purification and characterization of Proteins and Nucleic Acids

Course Outcomes






Describe the concepts of carbohydrates, lipids, nucleic acids, vitamins and minerals.



Explain concept of Bioenergetics including thermodynamics and enzymology.



Discuss the principles and operation of instruments for detecting biomolecules.



Explain the principles and application of separation and characterization of biomolecules from biological samples.



Identify chromatography techniques to separate molecules










FUNDAMENTAL OF STATISTICS



Course Overview

1. Help to understand the role of statistics in data analysis, decision-making, and scientific research
2. Introduce students to descriptive statistics, including measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and measures of dispersion (range, variance, standard deviation).
3. Teach students how to summarize and present data effectively using tables, charts, and graphs

Course Outcomes






Describe statistical population and sample, compile, classify and characterize data including scale of measurement.



Compile and present univariate data in tabular and graphical form and explain the descriptive statistics.



Compile and present bivariate data and explain it by various bivariate analysis, including the predictions/ forecasting.



Compute probability including events and distributions (normal, binomial, Poisson).



Explain the methods of hypothesis testing, parametric and non-parametric and use them to evaluate specific cases.










CO-CURRICULAR



Course Overview

Co-curricular activities will equip the students to enhance and engage with various sections of the society and formulate agendas of social and cultural events, seminars, workshops, awareness programs etc. It will also allow them to participate in community matters.
Course Outcomes






Students will learn to work well with others and communicate better.



Students will learn to manage their time and stay organized.



Students will enhance their creative abilities and think more critically.



Students will improve their overall health and reduce stress.



Students will become more aware of their role in society and contribute positively.

Even Semester

Courses for this
semester









ENDOCRINOLOGY AND IMMUNOLOGY



Course Overview

This course will help the students understand about the endocrine system, hormone action, and the receptors involved. The course also focuses on the role of immune cells, immunological responses, passive and active immunities, various immunogens, immunoglobulins, their role in keeping the body healthy and free of infections, production of vaccines based on the knowledge of immunogens, and adjuvants.
Course Outcomes






Identify various endocrine glands and their functions including biosynthesis and classification of hormones.



Describe endocrine, hypothalamus and their functions including invertebrate hormones.



Explain the types of immunity including functions of immune cells.



Explain the types of immunity including functions of immune cells.



Identify various immunoglobulins, their processing, presenting, activation and differentiation.










CELL BIOLOGY



Course Overview

Cell biology involves the study of structure and functions of the cell. Cell is basic functional unit of life and is indispensable part of tissue and organization of structure of any organism. The communication between cells is central to the functioning of any living organism.
Course Outcomes






Explain membrane structure and its functioning.



Describe structural organization of cell and their roles.



Illustrate different cell cycle processes.



Discuss mechanism of cell to cell communications.



Illustrate functions of cells and resulting diseases because their improper functioning.










MOLECULAR BIOLOGY , GENOMICS AND GENETIC ENGINEERING



Course Overview

The course of genomics and molecular biology includes understanding of DNA, RNA and protein molecule’s structure and variations. The course pays attention in understanding the minute events associated with central dogma of life starting from DNA being replicated to transcribed and ultimately translated. The Post transcriptional and post translational events are discussed in depth. The course also touches upon about mutation, mutagens and repair mechanisms.
Course Outcomes






Discuss genomics, genome, proteome and transcriptome.



Explain the central dogma including genome expression.



Illustrate genome sequencing, chromosome painting and genome mapping.



Explain DNA mutation and repair mechanisms.



Describe genetic engineering.

Year 2

















Odd Semester

Courses for this
semester









ANIMAL PHYSIOLOGY



Course Overview

Physiology is the study of the mechanics of the animal and human bodies studied at the molecular, cellular, tissue and organ levels. It will teach students to understand the physics and biochemistry of each organ system and how each of these systems contributes to the functioning of the body as a whole. The goal is to explain the fundamental mechanisms that operate in a living organism and how they interact.
Course Outcomes






Explain the concepts of gas exchange in the lungs and different types of respiratory pigments in humans and animals.



Describe the function of heart as a pump and the blood and lymph as connecting tissues to carry gases and nutrients to and from the tissues and heart.



Analyze the ways in which we response to stimuli along with the knowledge of how the brain stores and understands the information gathered to control our entire body.



Describe the breaking down of complex foods into nutrients that are necessary for our body, assimilation and elimination of the nitrogenous wastes.



Describe eye and ear as sensory organs and the visual-audio perception done by the brain.










DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY



Course Overview

The study of developmental biology includes basic knowledge of reproductive mechanisms of plants and animals. The study helps to understand gametogenesis, embryology, fertilization, post fertilization events, organogenesis, and production of adult organism. This subject provides the fundamental knowledge for animal biotechnology and stem cell research.
Course Outcomes






Recognize and explain the basic terminology of development, pre and post fertilization events and morphogenesis.



Explain gene regulations in axis and pattern formation in drosophila, amphibia and chick.



Explain and illustrate the process of organ formation (organogenesis).



Explain and illustrate the mechanism for regeneration of organs.



Explain metamorphosis and types of cell death.










AQUACULTURE



Course Overview

This course deals with different types of aquatic ecosystems and different types of aquaculture methods. It includes site selection criteria’s for aquaculture and prestocking and post stocking management processes.
Course Outcomes






Explain concepts of different aquatic ecosystems.



Illustrate types of aquaculture methods.



Access sites and identify species for aquaculture.



Explain and analyze pre stocking procedure and management.



Explain and analyze post stocking procedure and management.










ANIMAL DIVERSITY



Course Overview

The course will cover the knowledge regarding importance of biological diversity of the world. It provides an overview of Wildlife Protection Act, 1972. The course will also explain different adaptive capabilities of animal diversity.
Course Outcomes






Outline animal kingdom, classify and explain animal diversity.



Explain animal diversity in Indian context.



Describe salient features and composition of life forms.



Explain, illustrate and analyse adaptations in animal diversity.



Explain, illustrate conservation programme adopted in India for the conservation of wildlife.










RESEARCH ETHICS



Course Overview

The course will cover general concerns in research ethics as well as research ethics issues that may be specific to the candidate's own research. The general topics covered in the form of lectures are: Academic integrity including plagiarism, self-plagiarism. Research data and result bias, manipulation, and fabrication.
Course Outcomes






To be able to describe and apply theories and methods in ethics and research ethics.



To acquire an overview of important issues in research ethics, like responsibility for research, ethical vetting, and scientific misconduct.



To acquire skills of presenting arguments and results of ethical inquiries.



To be able to Identify the concepts and procedures of sampling, data collection, analysis and reporting.










MINI RESEARCH (SURVEY/EXPERIMENTS)-R3



Course Overview

The key aim is to seed the skills of the student to evaluate recent progress in a specific field, put research findings published in the preceding 1-2 years into a socio–research context, and explain future directions for research as appropriate. Also to build the ability of the Post Graduate Students to summarize the recent insights/advances in the specific research areas within the scope of Zoology.
Course Outcomes






Comprehend the format, style, layout, and depth of and mini-review.



Learn and understand meticulously the research report (Mini Review, Review, Research Article, etc.)



Prepare and Publish a mini-review in a peer-reviewed refereed, UGC care listed / Web of Science / Scopus / SCI / SCI Expanded / reputed indexed journals.










ORNAMENTAL FISH FARMING (TECHNO PROFESSIONAL SKILL II)



Course Overview

This paper deals with Identification of ornamental fishes and aquarium plants. It contains aquarium designing, setting up and maintenance of fresh water aquaria along with rearing of indigenous ornamental fish in aquaria. In covers estimation of physico chemical characteristcs of aquarium water, biological filter and culture of planktons.
Course Outcomes






Identify ornamental fish and aquarium plants.



Design setting up of aquaria and apply knowledge on farming for its maintenance.



Access rearing of indigenous ornamental fish.



Analyse and Evaluate physico-chemical characteristics of aquarium water and designs and construct biological filter for culturing plankton.



Access, analyse and revise (if required) ornamental fish farms through field visit.

RESEARCH/DATA ANALYSIS/DOCUMENTATION- R4



Course Overview

Research Problems in Entomology is a project-based faculty supervised research course. This course aims to give students hands-on laboratory or field experience that can be translated into career fields in entomology.
Course Outcomes






Students should demonstrate critical thinking skills through establishing methods to test a hypothesis



Students can analyse and interpret results and discuss findings



Students should demonstrate technical competency and ethical laboratory conduct



Students should be able to synthesize scientific literature to their experiments



Students can effectively communicate their finding to a scientific audience










ENTOMOLOGY I (INSECT BIOLOGY, ECOLOGY AND PEST MANAGEMENT)



Course Overview

The course will cover the knowledge regarding morphological and anatomical peculiarities found in different insect groups. It provides an overview of the defense mechanism of insects. It also emphasizes on different methods of insect pest management and vector borne diseases caused by insects.
Course Outcomes






Explain Class Insecta and describe morphology of insects



Illustrate and plan pest management approaches



Describe role of insects in an ecosystem



Describe the diseases caused by insects and their control measures



Explain defense mechanism of insects










ENTOMOLOGY II (INSECT PHYSIOLOGY AND TOXICOLOGY)



Course Overview

The course will cover the knowledge regarding different physiological processes operating in insect body. It provides an overview of the effects of neural system on other system of the insect body. It also emphasizes on pesticides and their mode of action in controlling insects.
Course Outcomes






Describe the endocrine system and their influence on physiology of insects



Explain physiological system of insects



Describe insect’s communication and its significance



Describe the toxicity of pesticides and their effects on insects



Identify pesticides and explain their mode of action in controlling insects










FISH BIOLOGY AND FISHERIES I (FISH PHYSIOLOGY AND FISH CULTURE)



Course Overview

This paper deals with basic knowledge of fisheries, general characteristics of fishes, feeding habit and digestion of fish, fish diseases and fisheries management.
Course Outcomes






Classify fish into appropriate groups based on their key characteristics



Describe respiration and excretion of fish



Discuss food and feeding habit of fishes and the digestive system of fishes



Explain types of fish diseases, their symptoms and control



Identify ornamental fishes of North East India and describe fish farming, fishing gears and crafts










FISH BIOLOGY AND FISHERIES II (FISH REPRODUCTIVE BIOLOGY, ENDOCRINOLOGY AND FISH GENETICS)



Course Overview

This paper deals with Sensory organs and migration of fishes, reproductive biology of fishes, endocrine system in fishes, modification in fishes, fish genetics and bioinformatics.
Course Outcomes






Explain concepts of sensory organs, pattern, and mechanism of fish migration



Describe the reproductive organs of fish



Explain Endocrine system in fishes



Compare the modifications of hill stream and deep sea fishes



Explain fish genetics and apply bioinformatics methods for managing data and retrieving meaningful information in connection to fishes
